patch_description:
Key changes:
- Reduced and structured parameterization: symmetry-grouped single-qubit rotations (corner/edge/center), shared CRZ ring and distinct center-edge CRZ, ZZZ motifs placed exactly on the eight winning lines (row/col/diag groups), CCRZ center interactions grouped by geometry, and shared post-RZ symmetry rotations. This yields 13 unique parameters per block → 13 * N_UPLOADS * N_REPEATS = 78 total parameters (compact and parameter-efficient).
- Geometric motif induction: placing ZZZ on winning lines and CCRZ interactions focused on center-edge/diagonal motifs encourages the ansatz to directly learn relevant three-body correlations for tic-tac-toe outcomes, improving generalization and sample efficiency.
- Heavy parameter sharing across symmetric board positions reduces overfitting (smaller train-test gap) while preserving expressive three-body and two-body entangling motifs.
- Training hyperparameters are unchanged (optimizer: Adam, default LR=0.03, early stopping with patience), so the candidate benefits from better inductive bias without tuning the learning schedule.

Expected effect:
- Lower parameter count and motif-aligned three-qubit interactions improve validation/test accuracy and reduce generalization gap compared to larger, less-structured blocks.
- Parameter sharing reduces depth/gate count relative to the current program and improves parameter efficiency.

Tunable parameters left for the outer training loop:
- learning_rate (default 0.03), n_epochs (default 100), steps_per_epoch (default 30), batch_size (default 15)
- early_stopping (default on), patience (default 75), min_delta (1e-4)

This proposal keeps the same inputs/outputs and training/evaluation protocol but supplies a more compact, symmetry- and motif-aware ANSATZ_SPEC.
